title: Atlas Lane Dossiers
boundary: Every Atlas box opens a dossier. Dossiers track public-record alignment, influence routes and evidence boundaries; they do not treat policy support, association, symbolism or office-holding as guilt.

lanes.title: People
lanes.examples: People layer overview
lanes.agendaRoute: Track public actors, offices and influence routes.
lanes.sources: Public office, documented leadership, public filings and official biographies.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Open politicians, financiers, intelligence figures and media-owner dossiers first.

lanes.title: Politicians
lanes.examples: Presidents, prime ministers, EU commissioners, security ministers, sanctions officials, migration ministers.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track public-record support, implementation or opposition to Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance policies, emergency powers, migration policy, sanctions and treaty routes.
lanes.sources: Official government leadership pages, parliamentary pages, ministerial pages, voting records, speeches, sanctions pages.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: A politician is not labelled as corrupt because they support SDGs or global policy. The dossier tracks public policy alignment, power route and records.

lanes.title: Financiers
lanes.examples: Central-bank chairs, IMF and World Bank leadership, asset-management CEOs, sovereign wealth leaders, bank regulators.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track monetary convergence, CBDC, digital identity, financial stability, asset-manager voting power, development finance and central-bank coordination.
lanes.sources: Official central-bank pages, IMF, World Bank, BIS, SEC, company leadership pages, filings and speeches.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: The key question is not “who is rich?” but who controls mandates, voting power, liquidity, standards, settlement rails and policy influence.

lanes.title: Intelligence figures
lanes.examples: CIA, ODNI, MI6, GCHQ, NSA, defence-intelligence, oversight committee figures, declassification officials.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track public leadership, declassification, oversight, intelligence reform, security doctrine, cyber authorities and public testimony.
lanes.sources: Official agency leadership pages, hearing records, inspector-general reports, declassified reading rooms.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Only public records and official roles are tracked. Private claims require primary records.

lanes.title: Media owners
lanes.examples: Media-company owners, chairmen, CEOs, controlling shareholders, platform executives and public editor leadership.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track ownership, narrative power, platform moderation, acquisition, board control, shareholder control and filing-confirmed influence.
lanes.sources: Company leadership pages, filings, ownership disclosures, annual reports and merger records.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: The dossier tracks ownership and editorial influence routes, not automatic mind-control claims.

lanes.title: Institutions
lanes.examples: Agencies, NGOs, banks, foundations, universities, media groups, courts, contractors, think tanks and standards bodies.
lanes.agendaRoute: Map institutional lanes that turn policy into money, rules, standards, grants, enforcement, research or public messaging.
lanes.sources: Official institution pages, annual reports, filings, grants, leadership pages and public records.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Institutions become meaningful when records show funding, office, contract, mandate or policy effect.

lanes.title: Agencies
lanes.examples: CIA, NSA, ODNI, DHS, DoD, FDA, CDC, Home Office, Frontex, Europol.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track public agency power, emergency authority, grants, rules, contracts, enforcement and release events.
lanes.sources: Official agency pages, reports, reading rooms, inspector-general pages.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Agency action should be read through official documents before commentary.

lanes.title: NGOs
lanes.examples: Humanitarian, policy, rights, migration, health and open-government groups.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track funding, program influence, partnerships, advocacy, field operations and public-policy effects.
lanes.sources: Official reports, annual reports, funding disclosures, charity records.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: NGO activity is not wrongdoing; the dossier tracks funding and policy route.

lanes.title: Banks and central banks
lanes.examples: Federal Reserve, ECB, BIS, IMF, World Bank, major banks and development banks.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track currency convergence, settlement systems, CBDC, lending, crisis response, stress tests and development finance.
lanes.sources: Official reports, financial statements, stress tests, lending reports, speeches and policy papers.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: The strongest evidence is official policy, implementation and money-flow records.

lanes.title: Foundations
lanes.examples: Large philanthropic foundations, policy foundations, donor-advised vehicles and research funders.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track grants, policy influence, education, health, media, research and NGO funding routes.
lanes.sources: Grant databases, annual reports, tax filings where available, charity registries.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Foundation support is a funding route, not proof of secret control without records.

lanes.title: Operations
lanes.examples: Wars, scandals, trials, covert-project allegations, sanctions, intelligence programs, procurement lanes and investigations.
lanes.agendaRoute: Map active operations only through public records, official statements and dated source trails.
lanes.sources: Official defence statements, court records, sanctions pages, FOIA libraries, public investigations.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Operations must be separated into proven, alleged, disputed and speculative.

lanes.title: Wars
lanes.examples: Ukraine, Gaza, Red Sea, Iran-linked escalation, Taiwan Strait pressure, Sahel conflict and civil wars.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track war as a convergence route: sanctions, energy, migration, defense contracts, casualties, diplomacy and media narrative.
lanes.sources: Official defence statements, UN OCHA, ICRC, court records, sanctions pages.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: War pages must separate civilian harm, military claims, source disputes and contractor/money routes.

lanes.title: Scandals
lanes.examples: Public-record scandals with court filings, regulator reports, settlements, committee reports and oversight records.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track scandal as a record chain: allegation, filing, response, settlement, regulator finding and missing proof.
lanes.sources: Court dockets, regulator releases, committee reports.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Scandal claims stay weak unless tied to documents.

lanes.title: Trials
lanes.examples: Criminal trials, civil suits, depositions, exhibits, appeals, sentencing and settlement hearings.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track legal process, not viral claims: parties, case numbers, exhibits, rulings and hearing dates.
lanes.sources: Court dockets, official judgments, PACER/CourtListener where applicable.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Trial pages should show what is alleged, what is proven and what remains contested.

lanes.title: Covert-project records
lanes.examples: Documented declassified programs, FOIA releases, reading-room files, inspector-general records and public admissions.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track only documented programs and declassified lanes; separate allegations from released records.
lanes.sources: CIA Reading Room, National Archives, agency FOIA libraries.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: No private covert claim is treated as settled without a record.

lanes.title: Money Flows
lanes.examples: Donations, contracts, grants, lobbying, foundations, procurement, shell structures, settlements, fines and compensation schemes.
lanes.agendaRoute: Trace money as the strongest path to power: who paid, who received, what for, when and under which authority.
lanes.sources: FEC, OpenSecrets, USAspending, EU tenders, procurement portals, filings and tax records.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Money-flow records often prove more than commentary.

lanes.title: Donations
lanes.examples: Campaign donations, PAC money, foundation gifts, university gifts and donor networks.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track donations as influence routes, not automatic bribery.
lanes.sources: FEC, OpenSecrets, tax filings, foundation reports, university disclosures.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: The record must show amount, date, recipient and purpose.

lanes.title: Contracts
lanes.examples: Defence, intelligence, cyber, AI, healthcare, border, logistics, reconstruction and emergency purchasing.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track contracts as operational control routes: vendor, agency, service, amount, period and outcome.
lanes.sources: USAspending, EU tenders, national procurement portals.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: This is a Tier 1 proof lane for the mission.

lanes.title: Grants
lanes.examples: Research, development, NGO, public-health, education and technology grants.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track grants as policy and influence routes across universities, NGOs, science, media and health.
lanes.sources: Grants.gov, EU Funding & Tenders, World Bank projects, foundation databases.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: The dossier should show funder, recipient, amount, program and public objective.

lanes.title: Lobbying
lanes.examples: Lobbying clients, firms, issue areas, bills, agencies contacted and foreign-principal filings.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track lobbying as public influence routing.
lanes.sources: LDA, FARA, EU Transparency Register.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Lobbying proves pressure route, not necessarily illegal conduct.

lanes.title: Legal Records
lanes.examples: Indictments, civil suits, depositions, hearings, exhibits, judgments, congressional records, FOIA releases and regulator findings.
lanes.agendaRoute: Evidence hierarchy lane: legal records outrank media and viral claims.
lanes.sources: Court records, DOJ releases, committee records, regulator findings.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Legal record pages must label allegation, evidence, finding and appeal status.

lanes.title: Indictments
lanes.examples: Charges, counts, defendants, prosecutors, alleged conduct, dates and case numbers.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track official charging documents and DOJ releases.
lanes.sources: Court dockets and DOJ releases.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: An indictment is an allegation until adjudicated.

lanes.title: Civil suits
lanes.examples: Complaints, parties, allegations, responses, settlements, dismissals and judgments.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track civil claims, filings and settlement boundaries.
lanes.sources: Court records, PACER, state courts, public dockets.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Settlement is not always admission; label the boundary.

lanes.title: Depositions and exhibits
lanes.examples: Transcript excerpts, exhibit numbers, admitted documents and sealed/unsealed status.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track primary record material and where it appears in the docket.
lanes.sources: Court filings and exhibit lists.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Never use deposition fragments without source context.

lanes.title: Hearings
lanes.examples: Congressional hearings, public inquiries, oversight hearings, regulator testimony and court hearings.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track official testimony, questions, documents and follow-up records.
lanes.sources: Committee pages, transcripts, video, court minutes.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Hearing claims need transcript or video links.

lanes.title: Symbolic Layer
lanes.examples: Mission patches, logos, ritual architecture, fraternal claims, occult aesthetics, language systems and public symbolism.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track symbolism as interpretation lane, not proof of conduct.
lanes.sources: Official image libraries, brand pages, heritage records, public archives.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Symbolism can guide commentary; it does not prove wrongdoing by itself.

lanes.title: Mission patches
lanes.examples: NASA, NRO, military, intelligence, space and public classified-program patches.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track official imagery, mission context, symbols and interpretation boundaries.
lanes.sources: Official image libraries and agency media pages.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Patch symbolism is commentary unless linked to public mission records.

lanes.title: Logos
lanes.examples: Agency seals, corporate marks, NGO marks, think-tank marks and institutional visual identity.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track logos and visual identity as public symbolic communication, not proof of agenda.
lanes.sources: Official brand and media-kit pages.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: The page should show official source, symbol reading and boundary.

lanes.title: Ritual architecture
lanes.examples: Courts, capitals, memorials, lodges, temples, monuments and ceremonial public spaces.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track public architecture, ritual use, heritage and symbolic design.
lanes.sources: Official heritage, building and institution pages.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Interpretation must remain labelled.

lanes.title: Fraternal claims
lanes.examples: Public lodge claims, official fraternal pages, public member lists and historical records.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track only public membership claims or official/historical records.
lanes.sources: Official fraternal/public archive pages.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Never infer private membership.

lanes.title: Human Cost
lanes.examples: Civilian casualties, migration, exploitation, vaccine compensation, displacement, food stress, medical collapse and war effects.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track power by consequence and method boundaries.
lanes.sources: UN, official ministries, courts, NGOs and compensation programs.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Numbers require definitions before figures.

lanes.title: Civilian casualties
lanes.examples: Deaths, injuries, missing, infrastructure destruction, undercount warnings and methodology differences.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track human cost of war and policy through source definitions.
lanes.sources: UN OCHA, ICRC, official ministries, court and NGO datasets.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Separate civilian, combatant, missing, indirect and disputed figures.

lanes.title: Migration
lanes.examples: Border encounters, asylum applications, removals, returns, overstays, deaths/missing and displacement.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track migration as human cost, policy route, NGO route, border contractor route and political signal.
lanes.sources: CBP/DHS, Frontex, Eurostat, Home Office, UNHCR, IOM.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Migration claims need definitions before conclusions.

lanes.title: Exploitation
lanes.examples: Forced labour, trafficking, child exploitation datasets, enforcement cases and support-service reports.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track exploitation with victim privacy boundaries and legal/source care.
lanes.sources: ILO, UNODC, courts, official enforcement pages.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Handle victims carefully; use official categories and court records.

lanes.title: Vaccine compensation
lanes.examples: Claims, compensated cases, denied cases, pending claims, legal standards and causation boundaries.
lanes.agendaRoute: Track compensation systems and legal standards, not unsupported causation claims.
lanes.sources: Official compensation programs and court records.
lanes.update: Weekly by default; faster during official releases, elections, filings, court events, crisis or sanctions changes.
lanes.boundary: Agenda 2030 / SDG / global-governance alignment is tracked as public-record policy alignment, not as proof of wrongdoing by itself.
conclusions: Compensation is a legal/administrative lane and must not be overstated.
